Thankyou 
Regards 
Malisha Fatima

I would have liked the opportunity to discuss the issues you raise especially given the length of time you say you've dealt with them on a number of your reviews. Still, hopefully, I can answer some of your queries below.

With over 8,000 patients at Uplands and record demand for appointments over the past two years, like all GP practices, we've really struggled, and we openly admit that.

When you only have so many appointments you can physically and safely deliver in a day, and demand outstrips supply; unfortunately, that means some patients won't be able to access the care they desperately need. That terrifying thought stays with each and every member of our team as we think of it happening to our own families, I can assure you.

At Uplands, our aim has always been to help as many patients as we can, as safely as we can, with the resources we have. We're not a big surgery, but we're big on trying to keep people well, just like Dr Quinn.

Staffing issues due to COVID, carefully caring for patients with COVID, staff being drafted in to work on the vaccination programmes, increasing levels of poor mental health amongst patients, long-standing national GP and nurse shortages, not to mention the hospital backlog, which has left many thousands of patients in fear and pain awaiting treatments and consultations...these have left GP practices on their knees.

We're so incredibly grateful for the patience and kindness showed to us while we endured the most challenging times ever in primary care, with some sadly still to come, I'm sure.

Our reception team are trained to ask patients for a brief outline of their symptoms to inform the GPs. The GPs then assess and decide who needs to be seen most urgently (known as triage), and it works a lot like A&E.

If the GP needs to see someone urgently, these are always same-day, by telephone or face to face if clinically appropriate. This continues to be for the safety and care of other vulnerable patients in the building, plus the ability to help as many people as we can in a day. Plus, most patients say it's much more convenient than coming down to the surgery for everything like before and leaving work/school.

If the GP decides it's safe to wait a few days, a routine telephone appointment is booked in the first instance. I fully appreciate the frustration of missing a callback. It's happened to me a couple of times with my own surgery.

The decision always sits with our clinicians, not the receptionists. I really hope that clears up some of your concerns, Mark and thank you for bringing things to our attention.

I appreciate you fed this back a few months ago now, but I would encourage you to discuss things further with me directly if you have time. Please phone and ask for me at the surgery: 0161 766 8221 or email me at: BUCCG.UplandsMedicalPractice@nhs.net and I'll do what I can to help.

You raise several points which I shall briefly try to respond to:
We no longer use AskMyGP but we do have new online services where you can request routine appointments within the next fortnight. Reception can give you the details and access.

Online services are the best for routine issues that don't need a same-day response. We can usually offer these within a few days.

We encourage patients to call us if they need to speak to a GP the same day. Our GPs can then assess your symptoms and decide how quickly you need to be seen.

As frustrating as it can be, our GPs try to give patients an idea of the time they'll call but, like you, cannot guarantee what they'll be doing. We always ask you to try and keep your phone close by and with a good signal when expecting a callback.

GPs are often faced with many issues that crop up at short notice. Emergencies where a patient needs to be admitted to hospital immediately, life-changing conversations where someone might be told they have a terminal illness or a patient with complex health needs where the GP needs to speak to a hospital consultant right away. These are just some of the most common ones. Even if you'd come in for a face to face appointment, you'd still need to wait in these instances.

Depending on the test results you're waiting for, we'll always tell you when to expect them and what to do if you don't receive them. I'm sorry; it doesn't sound like this happened for you, so please contact me if this hasn't been sorted yet.

Many thanks again and all the best, Kaneez - Sarah",null,[0,239]]]],[null,null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/reviews/data=!4m8!14m7!1m6!2m5!1sChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURxNzdDUXBnRRAB!2m1!1s0x0:0xdda5ea57eaa34e90!3m1!1s2@1:CIHM0ogKEICAgIDq77CQpgE%7C%7C?hl=en"],["https://www.google.com/local/content/rap/report?postId=ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURxNzdDUXBnRRAB&t=1&entityid=ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURxNzdDUXBnRRItChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURxNzdDUVpnEhNDZ3dJeUtyVmh3WVFpSXZBeGdNGi4KF0NJSE0wb2dLRUlDQWdJRHE3N0NRNWdFEhNDZ3dJeUtyVmh3WVFpSXZBeGdNIhIJAAAAAAAAAAARkE6j6lfqpd0qE0Nnd0l5S3JWaHdZUWlJdkF4Z00&wv=1&d=286732320",null,null,"0ahUKEwjK8Pf5ya2TAxUqdIQGHSK_HzsQoykIISgB"],null,[null,[[1,7]]]],"0ahUKEwjK8Pf5ya2TAxUqdIQGHSK_HzsQ0pMFCB8oCQ"],null,"CAESY0NBRVFlQnBFUTJwRlNVRlNTWEJEWjI5QlVEY3lTVlpDY1hSelIxOWZSV2hFUTFsSWEwUlRNSEZSVG1WMFJXTkNWVUZCUVVGQlIyZHVPVE5ZVlVOb1ZVZHhNbmRaV1VGRFNVRQ=="]]]

I'm extremely concerned to read about your experiences, especially regarding the nurse practitioner. I would like to understand more if you have time to contact me to discuss confidentially and directly at: BUCCG.UplandsMedicalPractice@nhs.net

We always aim to give excellent service to all our patients and try to demonstrate warmth, care and compassion in all of our interactions so we are saddened to hear of accounts of where our patients do not feel we get it right.

Increasingly, in general practice, we have a range of healthcare professionals working with us, which is great as it provides a massive range of skills and specialties within our team. Depending on your symptoms, urgency in the need to be seen and who we have available on the day you call, this might mean you don't always see the same person.

We know this can be frustrating for some patients, especially those with long-term health conditions. We will always try to match you with the same doctor or nurse for continuity of care wherever possible.

We know this to be an issue on your comments about the building itself. Sadly we are one of hundreds of practices in the region that need updates or new builds, but the national funding just isn't there to support this. Our aim is just to help as many patients as we can, as safely as we can, with the resources we have.

I do hope that helps but as I say, I am very happy to be contacted directly to discuss your concerns further. They still manage to remain helpful and professional and I do hope after your edit, you still find the same when you call. If you don't, I'd like to hear about it so I can look into it for you. My email is BUCCG.UplandsMedicalPractice@nhs.net.

In response to the other comments you raised, these may have changed since you left your review:
- You're right in that we don't do walk-in appointments; very few GP practices provide this that I'm aware of. All must be pre-booked.

- We take prescription requests over the telephone, online, via email and by post.

- I'm not 100% sure what you mean by outpatient services as these are traditionally offered at hospitals.

I can assure you our team never stops. On top of hundreds of urgent and routine appointments every week, there's hundreds upon hundreds of prescriptions to check and sign, care home visits, hospital referrals and letters, end of life care, complex long-term conditions work...our clinicians work flat out to see as many as they can in a day as well as do all the other duties expected of them.

If I can help with anything else, please don't hesitate to reach out to me.
Thanks,
